functions.name: Length
functions.docs: Returns the length of the warping.

functions.name: IsValid
functions.docs: Returns whether this warping transform is doing anything.

functions.name: GetRange
functions.docs: Returns a range that encompasses the whole warping time span.

functions.name: InverseFromWarp
functions.docs: Returns a transformation that takes us from a local time into a given loop back to the root time.

functions.name: TransformFrame
functions.signature: TransformFrame(Target, In Frame, Out Frame, Out Warp Index)
functions.docs: Transforms the given frame and returns the warped frame time along with the warp index we ended up in.

functions.name: TransformTime
functions.signature: TransformTime(Target, In Time, Out Time, Out Warp Index)
functions.docs: Transforms the given time and returns the warped time along with the warp index we ended up in.

functions.name: TransformTimeSpecific
functions.signature: TransformTimeSpecific(Target, In Time, Warp Count, Out Time)
functions.docs:
Transforms the given time by warping it by a specific warp count, regardless of how many warps are
needed in theory to stay in the warping range.

functions.name: TransformRangePure
functions.docs:
Transforms the given range in a "naive" way, i.e. its lower and upper bounds are transformed
independently by this time warping. This means that the output range could be "inside-out"... that is,
the output lower bound could be greater than the output upper bound, like, for instance, in the case
of the input range starting near the end of a loop, and ending near the beginning of another loop.

functions.name: TransformRangeUnwarped
functions.docs:
Transforms the given range by time-warping its lower bound, and computing an upper bound so that the
size of the input range is preserved. So if the input range starts in the middle of a loop and lasts
3 loops, the output range will start in the middle of the first loop, and last 3 times as long as
the Length of this time warp.

functions.name: TransformRangeConstrained
functions.docs:
Transforms the given range by time-warping it and figuring out if it "covered" a full loop or not.
If it covered a full loop, return a full-loop range, i.e. a range that goes from StartOffset to
(Length - EndOffset).
If it didn't cover a full loop, return the transformed range, which should be a subset of the full
loop range mentioned above.

functions.docs: Convert a FMovieSceneTimeWarping into a string
